dossier.public_summary: The dip depth changes by a factor of five between sectors and between individual transits, from 446 ppm to 2412 ppm, and the folded light curve is V-shaped. A planet must always have the same depth, so this is best explained by stellar variability or a blended binary eclipse, not a transiting planet.

reasons.why: Depth changes enormously between sectors, from 446 ppm in sector 24 to 2412 ppm in sector 50 and 2046 ppm in sector 51. This is 131.3% change and cannot be a planet on the target.
The depth instability is within the same SPOC 2-min product (3 sectors, depth 1102 +/- 95 ppm), so it is not a calibration difference between pipelines.

Single-transit depths are wildly inconsistent; the signal is driven by two deep transits in 2022 (sectors 50/51) and an undetected shallow transit in sector 24, with near_gap=5 and p_chance=0.003016, the hallmark of a few bad events or systematics rather than a consistent planet.

reasons.why: The folded shape is V-shaped with ingress fraction at the boundary (0.5) implying a long duration well beyond the central duration for the host, favoring a stellar/eclipsing signal, and the centroid is inconclusive so an on-target binary cannot be excluded.
